category: Statistics and Machine Learning Toolbox > Classification, Clustering & Model Assessment
description: Supervised classifiers, unsupervised clustering and dimensionality reduction, feature selection, and the cross-validation and performance-evaluation functions used to assess them.

tools.name: fitctree
tools.description: Grow a binary classification decision tree by recursive partitioning on predictor values. Trees are highly interpretable, need no feature scaling, and handle categorical predictors and missing data via surrogate splits. Control overfitting with MinLeafSize, MaxNumSplits or post-hoc pruning.
tools.usage:
tree = fitctree(Tbl, ResponseVarName)
tree = fitctree(X, Y)
tree = fitctree(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'MinLeafSize' / 'MinParentSize'
parameters.description: Minimum observations in a leaf or before a split is attempted.

parameters.name: 'Prune' / 'PruneCriterion'
parameters.description: Enable cost-complexity pruning and choose its criterion.

parameters.name: 'ClassNames' / 'Prior' / 'Cost'
parameters.description: Class ordering, prior probabilities and misclassification cost matrix.

tools.notes: Use prune(tree, 'Level', k) to simplify, and predictorImportance(tree) to rank features.

tools.name: fitcsvm
tools.description: Train a binary support vector machine classifier with linear, Gaussian or polynomial kernels, or a one-class SVM for anomaly detection. Maximizing the margin gives good generalization on small to medium datasets. Kernel scale and box constraint are the critical hyperparameters and usually need tuning.
tools.usage:
Mdl = fitcsvm(Tbl, ResponseVarName)
Mdl = fitcsvm(X, Y)
Mdl = fitcsvm(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'KernelFunction'
parameters.description: 'linear' (default for two classes), 'gaussian'/'rbf', 'polynomial', or a custom function.

parameters.name: 'KernelScale'
parameters.description: Numeric scale or 'auto' for a data-driven heuristic.

parameters.name: 'BoxConstraint'
parameters.description: Regularization parameter C; larger fits the training data harder.

parameters.name: 'Standardize'
parameters.description: Logical; essential for RBF kernels on unscaled data.

parameters.name: 'OutlierFraction'
parameters.description: Expected fraction of outliers, used with one-class SVM.

parameters.name: 'OptimizeHyperparameters'
parameters.description: 'auto' to run Bayesian optimization on the key parameters.

tools.notes: fitcsvm handles only two classes; wrap it in fitcecoc for multiclass problems.

tools.name: fitcecoc
tools.description: Train a multiclass classifier by reducing the problem to a set of binary problems using an error-correcting output codes scheme. Any binary learner can be plugged in via a template, most commonly an SVM. It is the standard way to apply SVMs to more than two classes.
tools.usage:
Mdl = fitcecoc(Tbl, ResponseVarName)
Mdl = fitcecoc(X, Y)
Mdl = fitcecoc(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'Learners'
parameters.description: A template such as templateSVM, templateTree or templateLinear, or a cell array of them.

parameters.name: 'FitPosterior'
parameters.description: Logical; transform scores into class posterior probabilities.

parameters.name: 'Options'
parameters.description: statset('UseParallel', true) to train binary learners in parallel.

tools.name: fitcknn
tools.description: Train a k-nearest-neighbour classifier, which classifies a point by majority vote among its k closest training points. There is no real training phase, so it is instant to fit but slower to predict on large datasets. Distance metric, k and distance weighting are the parameters that matter.
tools.usage:
Mdl = fitcknn(Tbl, ResponseVarName)
Mdl = fitcknn(X, Y)
Mdl = fitcknn(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'Standardize'
parameters.description: Logical; almost always needed because kNN is scale-sensitive.

tools.name: fitcnb
tools.description: Train a naive Bayes classifier that models each predictor as conditionally independent given the class. Despite the strong independence assumption it works remarkably well for text and high-dimensional data and trains in a single pass. Choose the per-predictor distribution: normal, kernel, multinomial or multivariate multinomial.
tools.usage:
Mdl = fitcnb(Tbl, ResponseVarName)
Mdl = fitcnb(X, Y)
Mdl = fitcnb(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'DistributionNames'
parameters.description: 'normal' (default), 'kernel', 'mn' (multinomial, for word counts), 'mvmn' (categorical), or a per-predictor cell array.

parameters.name: 'Prior'
parameters.description: 'empirical' (default), 'uniform' or a vector of prior probabilities.

tools.notes: A zero-variance predictor within a class makes the 'normal' option fail; switch that predictor to 'kernel'.

tools.name: fitcdiscr
tools.description: Fit a linear or quadratic discriminant analysis classifier, which models each class as multivariate normal. LDA assumes a shared covariance matrix and gives linear boundaries; QDA estimates one per class and gives curved boundaries. Regularization via Gamma and Delta handles ill-conditioned or high-dimensional covariance estimates.
tools.usage:
Mdl = fitcdiscr(Tbl, ResponseVarName)
Mdl = fitcdiscr(X, Y)
Mdl = fitcdiscr(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'Gamma'
parameters.description: Regularization of the covariance matrix, 0 to 1.

parameters.name: 'Delta'
parameters.description: Linear coefficient threshold for feature elimination.

parameters.name: 'Prior' / 'Cost'
parameters.description: Class priors and misclassification cost matrix.

tools.name: fitclinear
tools.description: Train a linear classifier (SVM or logistic regression) on high-dimensional data using stochastic gradient and quasi-Newton solvers with ridge or lasso regularization. It is designed for datasets with many thousands of features such as text bag-of-words. Supports parallel and incremental workflows.
tools.usage:
Mdl = fitclinear(X, Y)
Mdl = fitclinear(Tbl, ResponseVarName)
[Mdl, FitInfo, HyperparameterOptimizationResults] = fitclinear(___, Name, Value)

tools.name: fitcensemble
tools.description: Train an ensemble of classification learners with boosting (AdaBoost, LogitBoost, GentleBoost, RUSBoost) or bagging. Boosted shallow trees are usually the strongest general-purpose tabular classifier available. RUSBoost is specifically designed for heavily imbalanced classes.
tools.usage:
Mdl = fitcensemble(Tbl, ResponseVarName)
Mdl = fitcensemble(X, Y)
Mdl = fitcensemble(___, Name, Value)
tools.example:
load ionosphere
rng(1)
t = templateTree('MaxNumSplits', 10);
Mdl = fitcensemble(X, Y, 'Method', 'AdaBoostM1', ...
    'NumLearningCycles', 200, 'Learners', t, 'LearnRate', 0.1);
plot(loss(Mdl, X, Y, 'mode', 'cumulative'))
xlabel('Number of trees'), ylabel('Classification error')

tools.name: TreeBagger
tools.description: Build a random forest by bootstrap-aggregating decision trees with random predictor selection at each split. It provides out-of-bag error estimates and out-of-bag predictor importance for free, with no separate validation set needed. Works for both classification and regression.
tools.usage:
Mdl = TreeBagger(NumTrees, Tbl, ResponseVarName)
Mdl = TreeBagger(NumTrees, X, Y)
Mdl = TreeBagger(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: NumTrees
parameters.description: Number of trees to grow; more is always safer, just slower.

parameters.name: 'NumPredictorsToSample'
parameters.description: Features considered per split; default sqrt(p) for classification.

parameters.name: 'MinLeafSize'
parameters.description: Minimum leaf size (1 for classification, 5 for regression).

tools.example:
load ionosphere
rng(0)
B = TreeBagger(200, X, Y, 'Method', 'classification', ...
    'OOBPrediction', 'on', 'OOBPredictorImportance', 'on');
plot(oobError(B)); xlabel('Trees'), ylabel('OOB error')
figure, bar(B.OOBPermutedPredictorDeltaError)
tools.notes: fitcensemble(..., 'Method', 'Bag') gives a similar model in the newer object framework.

tools.name: templateTree
tools.description: Create a decision tree template that configures the weak learners used inside an ensemble. It accepts the same options as fitctree/fitrtree but does not fit anything on its own. Controlling MaxNumSplits through a template is the main way to tune boosting performance.
tools.usage:
t = templateTree()
t = templateTree(Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'MaxNumSplits'
parameters.description: Tree depth control; 1 gives decision stumps.

parameters.name: 'NumVariablesToSample'
parameters.description: Features considered per split ('all' for boosting, sqrt(p) for bagging).

parameters.name: 'Surrogate'
parameters.description: 'on' to handle missing values and improve importance estimates.

tools.name: kmeans
tools.description: Partition data into k clusters by minimizing within-cluster sums of point-to-centroid distances. It returns cluster indices, centroid locations, within-cluster sums and per-point distances. Because the result depends on the random initialization, use several replicates and the k-means++ start.
tools.usage:
idx = kmeans(X, k)
[idx, C] = kmeans(X, k)
[idx, C, sumd, D] = kmeans(X, k, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'Replicates'
parameters.description: Number of random restarts; the best solution is kept.

parameters.name: 'Options'
parameters.description: statset('UseParallel', true) to run replicates in parallel.

tools.notes: Standardize the data first when variables have different units. Use evalclusters or silhouette to choose k.

tools.name: kmedoids
tools.description: Partition data into k clusters whose centres are actual data points (medoids) rather than means. This makes it robust to outliers and usable with any distance metric, including non-Euclidean ones. Use it when the mean is not meaningful or when you need a representative real exemplar per cluster.
tools.usage:
idx = kmedoids(X, k)
[idx, C, sumd, D, midx, info] = kmedoids(X, k, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'Distance'
parameters.description: Any pdist metric, or a custom distance function handle.

parameters.name: midx
parameters.description: Row indices in X of the chosen medoids.

tools.name: dbscan
tools.description: Density-based clustering that groups points with at least minpts neighbours within radius epsilon, marking sparse points as noise (index -1). It finds clusters of arbitrary shape and determines the number of clusters automatically. Choosing epsilon from a k-distance plot is the usual tuning procedure.
tools.usage:
idx = dbscan(X, epsilon, minpts)
idx = dbscan(D, epsilon, minpts, 'Distance', 'precomputed')
[idx, corepts] = dbscan(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: minpts
parameters.description: Minimum neighbours (including the point) for a core point; a common rule is 2*ndims.

parameters.name: 'Distance'
parameters.description: Any pdist metric, or 'precomputed' with a distance matrix.

tools.name: pdist
tools.description: Compute pairwise distances between all observations, returned in compact vector form. It supports more than a dozen metrics including Euclidean, Mahalanobis, cosine, correlation, Jaccard and custom functions. Its output feeds linkage, mdscale and other distance-based methods.
tools.usage:
D = pdist(X)
D = pdist(X, metric)
D = pdist(X, 'minkowski', p)
D = pdist(X, @distfun)
tools.notes: Use squareform to convert between the compact vector and a full symmetric matrix. pdist2 computes distances between two different sets.

tools.name: linkage
tools.description: Build an agglomerative hierarchical cluster tree from a distance vector or a data matrix. The linkage method determines how inter-cluster distance is measured, with Ward's method usually producing the most balanced clusters. The output encodes the whole merge history so you can cut the tree at any level later.
tools.usage:
Z = linkage(X)
Z = linkage(X, method)
Z = linkage(X, method, metric)
Z = linkage(D, method)

parameters.name: metric
parameters.description: Distance metric when X is raw data.

parameters.name: 'savememory'
parameters.description: 'on' or 'off'; 'on' avoids forming the full distance matrix.

tools.notes: 'ward', 'centroid' and 'median' are only meaningful with Euclidean distance.

tools.name: cluster
tools.description: Cut a hierarchical cluster tree to produce flat cluster assignments, either by specifying the number of clusters or an inconsistency/distance cutoff. It is the step that turns a dendrogram into usable labels. Use MaxClust when you know how many groups you want and Cutoff when you do not.
tools.usage:
T = cluster(Z, 'MaxClust', n)
T = cluster(Z, 'Cutoff', c)
T = cluster(Z, 'Cutoff', c, 'Criterion', criterion)

parameters.name: 'MaxClust'
parameters.description: Maximum number of clusters to form.

tools.name: dendrogram
tools.description: Plot a hierarchical cluster tree as a dendrogram, optionally collapsing the tree to a maximum number of leaf nodes. A colour threshold highlights distinct clusters below a given merge height. It returns the line handles and the leaf-to-observation mapping.
tools.usage:
dendrogram(Z)
dendrogram(Z, P)
[H, T, outperm] = dendrogram(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: P
parameters.description: Maximum number of leaf nodes to show (default 30; 0 shows all).

parameters.name: 'ColorThreshold'
parameters.description: Height below which branches get distinct colours, or 'default'.

tools.name: evalclusters
tools.description: Evaluate clustering solutions over a range of cluster counts using the Calinski-Harabasz, Davies-Bouldin, gap or silhouette criterion, and report the optimal number of clusters. It can run the clustering itself given an algorithm name, or evaluate precomputed labels. Use it to choose k objectively rather than by eye.
tools.usage:
eva = evalclusters(X, clust, criterion)
eva = evalclusters(X, clust, criterion, 'KList', klist)
eva = evalclusters(X, clustFun, criterion, Name, Value)

parameters.name: clust
parameters.description: 'kmeans', 'linkage', 'gmdistribution', a function handle, or a matrix of precomputed labels.

parameters.name: 'KList'
parameters.description: Vector of cluster counts to evaluate.

parameters.name: 'Distance'
parameters.description: Distance metric for silhouette and gap criteria.

tools.name: silhouette
tools.description: Compute and plot silhouette values, which measure for each point how close it is to its own cluster relative to the nearest other cluster. Values near 1 mean a confident assignment, near 0 a boundary case, and negative values a likely misassignment. The mean silhouette is a common cluster-quality score.
tools.usage:
silhouette(X, clust)
s = silhouette(X, clust, metric)
[s, h] = silhouette(___)

parameters.name: metric
parameters.description: Distance metric, or a custom function handle.

tools.name: fitgmdist
tools.description: Fit a Gaussian mixture model by expectation-maximization, giving soft cluster memberships and a generative density estimate. Unlike k-means it models cluster shape through covariance matrices and returns posterior probabilities. Regularization and multiple replicates are usually needed for stable fits.
tools.usage:
GMModel = fitgmdist(X, k)
GMModel = fitgmdist(X, k, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'SharedCovariance'
parameters.description: Logical; force all components to share one covariance.

parameters.name: 'RegularizationValue'
parameters.description: Small value added to covariance diagonals to avoid singularity.

tools.name: pca
tools.description: Perform principal component analysis, returning the component coefficients (loadings), the transformed scores, the eigenvalues and the percentage of variance explained. It is the standard linear dimensionality-reduction and decorrelation technique. Centre and usually standardize the data first when variables have different units.
tools.usage:
coeff = pca(X)
[coeff, score, latent] = pca(X)
[coeff, score, latent, tsquared, explained, mu] = pca(X, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'VariableWeights'
parameters.description: Set to 'variance' to work from the correlation matrix.

tools.notes: score = (X - mu) * coeff. Use pcares for residuals and ppca for probabilistic PCA with missing data.

tools.name: tsne
tools.description: Reduce high-dimensional data to two or three dimensions with t-distributed stochastic neighbour embedding, preserving local neighbourhood structure for visualization. Cluster separation in a t-SNE plot is meaningful but distances between clusters and cluster sizes are not. Perplexity and the exaggeration factor are the main tuning knobs.
tools.usage:
Y = tsne(X)
[Y, loss] = tsne(X, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'Perplexity'
parameters.description: Effective number of neighbours (default 30); lower emphasizes local structure.

parameters.name: 'Distance'
parameters.description: Any pdist metric or a custom function.

tools.notes: Results change with the random seed; always set rng for reproducibility. Never use t-SNE coordinates as features for a downstream model.

tools.name: cvpartition
tools.description: Create a cross-validation partition object defining k-fold, holdout, leave-one-out or resubstitution splits. Stratification preserves class proportions in every fold, and grouping keeps related observations together. Reuse the same partition across models so comparisons are fair.
tools.usage:
c = cvpartition(n, 'KFold', k)
c = cvpartition(group, 'KFold', k)
c = cvpartition(n, 'HoldOut', p)
c = cvpartition(n, 'LeaveOut')
idxTrain = training(c, i); idxTest = test(c, i)

parameters.name: n / group
parameters.description: Number of observations, or a grouping vector for stratified partitioning.

parameters.name: 'HoldOut'
parameters.description: Fraction (or count) held out for testing.

parameters.name: 'Stratify'
parameters.description: Logical; true by default when a grouping variable is supplied.

tools.name: crossval
tools.description: Estimate the generalization loss of a model by cross-validation, either by partitioning an already fitted model or by running arbitrary train and test function handles. The partitioned-model form returns a cross-validated model object you then query with kfoldLoss or kfoldPredict. Use the function-handle form for custom pipelines.
tools.usage:
CVMdl = crossval(Mdl)
CVMdl = crossval(Mdl, 'KFold', k)
vals = crossval(fun, X)
vals = crossval(criterion, X, y, 'Predfun', predfun, 'KFold', k)

parameters.name: Mdl
parameters.description: A fitted classification or regression model object.

parameters.name: 'Predfun'
parameters.description: Function handle @(Xtrain, ytrain, Xtest) returning predictions.

parameters.name: 'MCReps'
parameters.description: Monte Carlo repetitions for holdout validation.

tools.name: kfoldLoss
tools.description: Compute the cross-validated loss (classification error, MSE or another criterion) from a partitioned model object. It aggregates the out-of-fold predictions, giving an honest estimate of generalization performance. Per-fold losses are available with the 'Mode' option.
tools.usage:
L = kfoldLoss(CVMdl)
L = kfoldLoss(CVMdl, Name, Value)

parameters.name: CVMdl
parameters.description: A cross-validated model from crossval or from fitting with 'KFold'.

tools.name: loss
tools.description: Evaluate the loss of a trained model on supplied test data and true labels. The loss function can be changed to hinge, deviance, exponential or a custom handle, and ensembles can report cumulative loss across learners. Use it for held-out evaluation once a model is trained.
tools.usage:
L = loss(Mdl, X, Y)
L = loss(Mdl, Tbl, ResponseVarName)
L = loss(___, Name, Value)

tools.name: confusionmat
tools.description: Compute the confusion matrix comparing known and predicted class labels, with rows for true classes and columns for predicted ones. The second output returns the class order, which you need to interpret the matrix. It is the basis for precision, recall and F1 calculations.
tools.usage:
C = confusionmat(group, grouphat)
[C, order] = confusionmat(group, grouphat)
C = confusionmat(___, 'Order', order)

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: True labels (numeric, categorical, string or cell array of char).

parameters.name: 'Order'
parameters.description: Explicit class ordering for the matrix rows/columns.

tools.name: confusionchart
tools.description: Display a confusion matrix as an annotated chart with optional row and column summaries showing per-class recall and precision. Normalization options let you show percentages instead of counts. It is the clearest way to present multiclass classification results.
tools.usage:
confusionchart(trueLabels, predictedLabels)
confusionchart(m)
confusionchart(m, classLabels)
cm = confusionchart(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'ColumnSummary'
parameters.description: Same options, shown below the chart.

tools.name: perfcurve
tools.description: Compute an ROC curve (or precision-recall, or other performance curve) from classifier scores, together with the area under the curve and optimal operating point. Confidence bounds can be obtained by bootstrap or from cross-validated scores. Use it to compare classifiers independently of a particular decision threshold.
tools.usage:
[X, Y] = perfcurve(labels, scores, posclass)
[X, Y, T, AUC] = perfcurve(___)
[X, Y, T, AUC, OPTROCPT] = perfcurve(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: posclass
parameters.description: The label treated as the positive class.

parameters.name: 'XCrit' / 'YCrit'
parameters.description: Criteria for the axes: 'fpr', 'tpr', 'prec', 'reca', 'accu', 'fnr' and others.

parameters.name: 'Cost'
parameters.description: Misclassification cost matrix used to find the optimal point.

tools.notes: rocmetrics provides an object-based interface that handles multiclass ROC analysis in one call.

tools.name: relieff
tools.description: Rank predictors by importance using the RReliefF (regression) or ReliefF (classification) algorithm, which rewards features that distinguish nearby observations of different classes. Unlike univariate filters it accounts for feature interactions and local structure. Returns the ranking and the per-feature weights.
tools.usage:
[idx, weights] = relieff(X, y, k)
[idx, weights] = relieff(X, y, k, Name, Value)

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Number of nearest neighbours to consider; larger is more robust to noise.

parameters.name: 'method'
parameters.description: 'classification' or 'regression'; inferred from y by default.

parameters.name: 'sigma'
parameters.description: Distance scaling for the neighbour weighting.

tools.notes: fscmrmr, fscchi2 and fsrftest are alternative filter-based feature ranking functions.

tools.name: sequentialfs
tools.description: Select features sequentially (forward or backward) by minimizing a cross-validated criterion you define with a function handle. Because the criterion is arbitrary, it works for any model type. Be aware that wrapper selection is computationally expensive and can overfit if the criterion is not cross-validated.
tools.usage:
inmodel = sequentialfs(fun, X, y)
[inmodel, history] = sequentialfs(fun, X, y, Name, Value)

parameters.name: fun
parameters.description: Handle @(Xtrain, ytrain, Xtest, ytest) returning the criterion value (e.g. number of errors).

parameters.name: 'cv'
parameters.description: A cvpartition, a fold count, or 'none'.

parameters.name: 'nfeatures'
parameters.description: Exact number of features to select.

tools.name: predictorImportance
tools.description: Estimate the relative importance of each predictor in a fitted tree or ensemble by summing the change in node risk attributable to splits on that predictor. It gives a fast, model-based feature ranking without refitting. For ensembles a second output gives the per-learner contributions.
tools.usage:
imp = predictorImportance(tree)
[imp, ma] = predictorImportance(ens)

parameters.name: tree / ens
parameters.description: A fitted ClassificationTree, RegressionTree or ensemble model.

tools.notes: Impurity-based importance is biased toward high-cardinality predictors; TreeBagger's out-of-bag permutation importance is less biased.

tools.name: classificationLearner
tools.description: Open the Classification Learner app, which trains and compares many classifier types interactively with automatic cross-validation, feature selection and hyperparameter optimization. The best model can be exported to the workspace or generated as MATLAB code. It is the fastest way to survey which model family suits a dataset.
tools.usage:
classificationLearner
classificationLearner(Tbl, ResponseVarName)
classificationLearner(X, Y)
classificationLearner(___, 'HoldOut', p)

parameters.name: Tbl / X, Y
parameters.description: Training data as a table or predictor matrix plus labels.

parameters.name: 'KFold' / 'HoldOut'
parameters.description: Validation scheme to use in the session.

tools.notes: regressionLearner is the equivalent app for regression problems.
